Fungal infection.d: A skin infection caused by fungi, often red and itchy.

Allergy.d: An immune reaction to a trigger such as pollen, dust or food.

GERD.d: Stomach acid flows back into the food pipe, causing heartburn.
p: Avoid lying down right after eating
Limit spicy, fatty food and caffeine

Chronic cholestasis.d: Reduced bile flow from the liver, often with itching and yellow skin.

Drug Reaction.d: An unwanted reaction to a medicine, such as rash or swelling.
p: Do not retake it until a doctor reviews it
Seek help at once for swelling or breathing trouble

Peptic ulcer diseae.d: Sores in the stomach or upper gut lining that cause burning pain.

AIDS.d: Advanced HIV infection that weakens the immune system.
p: Keep up regular check-ups and vaccinations

Diabetes.d: A condition in which blood sugar stays too high.
p: Limit sugary food and stay active

Gastroenteritis.d: A stomach and gut infection causing vomiting and diarrhoea.
p: Sip fluids or oral rehydration solution

Bronchial Asthma.d: Airways narrow and swell, causing wheeze and breathlessness.
p: Avoid triggers like smoke and dust

Hypertension.d: Long-term high blood pressure that strains the heart and vessels.

Migraine.d: Recurring severe headaches, often with nausea and light sensitivity.
p: Rest in a dark, quiet room

Cervical spondylosis.d: Age-related wear of the neck bones and discs, causing neck pain.
p: Avoid long spells looking down at screens

Paralysis (brain hemorrhage).d: Loss of movement linked to bleeding in the brain, a medical emergency.

Jaundice.d: Yellowing of the skin and eyes from excess bilirubin, often a liver problem.

Malaria.d: A mosquito-borne parasite infection causing fever and chills.

Chicken pox.d: A contagious viral illness with an itchy blister rash.
p: Stay home until blisters crust over
Keep away from pregnant women and newborns

Dengue.d: A mosquito-borne viral fever that can cause severe pain and low platelets.
p: Rest and drink plenty of fluids
Avoid aspirin and ibuprofen unless a doctor says so

Typhoid.d: A bacterial infection from contaminated food or water, with long-lasting fever.

hepatitis A.d: A liver infection spread through contaminated food or water.

Hepatitis B.d: A liver infection spread through blood and body fluids.

Hepatitis C.d: A liver infection spread mainly through blood.

Hepatitis D.d: A liver infection that only occurs together with hepatitis B.

Hepatitis E.d: A liver infection spread through contaminated water.

Alcoholic hepatitis.d: Liver inflammation caused by heavy drinking.

Tuberculosis.d: A bacterial lung infection that spreads through the air.
p: Take the full course of medicine

Common Cold.d: A mild viral infection of the nose and throat.
p: Use steam or saline spray for a blocked nose

Pneumonia.d: An infection that inflames the air sacs in the lungs.

Dimorphic hemmorhoids(piles).d: Swollen veins in the rectum or anus that cause pain or bleeding.
p: Eat more fibre and drink water
Do not sit for long periods

Heart attack.d: Blocked blood flow to the heart, a medical emergency.
p: Sit down and stay calm until help arrives
Do not drive yourself to hospital

Varicose veins.d: Twisted, enlarged veins, usually in the legs.

Hypothyroidism.d: An underactive thyroid causing tiredness and weight gain.

Hyperthyroidism.d: An overactive thyroid causing weight loss and a fast heartbeat.

Hypoglycemia.d: Low blood sugar causing shakiness, sweating and confusion.
p: Take fast-acting sugar such as juice

Osteoarthristis.d: Wear of joint cartilage causing pain and stiffness.
p: Use heat or cold packs for pain

Arthritis.d: Inflammation of the joints causing pain and swelling.

(vertigo) Paroymsal Positional Vertigo.d: Brief spinning dizziness triggered by head movements.

Acne.d: Blocked skin pores causing pimples and blackheads.
p: Wash your face gently twice a day

Urinary tract infection.d: A bacterial infection of the bladder or urinary tract.

Psoriasis.d: A skin condition causing red, scaly patches.

Impetigo.d: A contagious bacterial skin infection with crusty sores.
